title: routing-memory-sweep-experiment-log
content:
Purpose:
This is a working log of targeted micro‑experiments that surfaced a repeatable latency and memory amplification pattern when serving long contexts across different model families (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and with a gated MoE routing layer. Goal is to capture raw observations, minimal repro configs, quick hypotheses, and actionable next steps for the runtime and compilation teams.

Background / why this matters:
- Customers are moving to 32k+ contexts and we see cost/latency spikes that aren't explained by token count alone.
- Symptoms: sudden memory jumps on step N (not first token), degraded CPU/GPU utilization, and long GC pauses in the Python runtime on dedicated infra.
- Affects: hosted API and dedicated pools when using: a) large attention window policies, b) MoE-enabled checkpoints, c) models with different kv-cache layout (Qwen vs Llama).

High-level hypothesis summary (short):
1) MoE router state + per-expert KV cache shards cause periodic reallocation and copy amplification for long prefixes.
2) Certain attention kernel codepaths (Mistral optimized transformer blocks) use fused ops that allocate transient tensors for causal mask handling at >8k sequence lengths.
3) Qwen's attention layout (packed head dimension) interacts poorly with our continuous batching and KV slice copying logic, causing extra memcpy when routing between devices.

Environment (minimal repro):
- Runtime: rwd-served 2.7.1 (dev build with debug traces enabled)
- Hardware: A100-40GB, 8-vCPU host, 1 worker process per GPU (isolated test node)
- Python: 3.10.11, CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 8.8
- Models tested: llama-70b-v1 (fp16), mistral-22b-v1 (fp16), qwen-14b-v1 (int8/FP16 mix)
- MoE: synthetic moa-2-expert wrapper to emulate gated dispatch and per-expert KV slices
- Load: single-stream long prefix generation (prefix=24k tokens, generate 2k tokens), continuous batching disabled

Quick experiment matrix (configs and observed artifact):
- EXP-A: llama-70b, no-MoE, kv-cache standard -> baseline latency 1.0x, memory delta linear with tokens
- EXP-B: llama-70b, +MoE (2 experts), router on CPU -> latency 1.35x at step ~3k; observed host-side memcpy spikes (trace id 1003)
- EXP-C: mistral-22b, no-MoE, fused-attn on -> 1.1x latency but spikes in transient GPU allocations at ~8k boundary
- EXP-D: qwen-14b, +MoE, router pinned to GPU -> worst memory amplification 2.1x and periodic CUDA streams stall
- EXP-E: qwen-14b, no-MoE, continuous batch windowing enabled -> lower latency but higher tail variance when prefix crosses 16k

Representative trace excerpts (translated from raw trace events):
- trace#1003 (EXP-B): host memcpy 1.2GB @ t=3.2s, followed by 0.6s CPU busy loop for router scheduling; GPU utilization dips from 98%->22%
- trace#1009 (EXP-D): cudaMemAlloc transient 512MB chunks repeatedly at t=9.0s..9.8s; stream syncs observed between dispatch and next-token kernel

Micro-observations and notes (informal):
- When MoE routing is on, we see router decision structures (per-token) serialized into host memory and then copied to device for dispatch. That copy footprint grows with active experts and is amplified by our current 'pack-and-send' for KV updates.
- Llama's KV layout is 2D contiguous and the runtime handles slices with a single view; Qwen uses interleaved head packing that forces our code to create a temporary contiguous buffer before cudaMemcpy (extra copy).
- Mistral fused-attn path allocates a causal-mask tensor sized O(seq_len^2) in the intermediate path when sequence crosses implementation threshold; this appears to be a compiled kernel fallback that wasn't present in smaller sequences.
- GC/allocator pressure: Python allocator shows large free list churn; observed 30–60s latency tail from occasional 'scoped garbage collect' calls when serving many long prefix requests back-to-back.

Immediate concrete repro steps for eng: (copy/paste runnable)
1) checkout branch rwd/diagnostics/memory-sweep
2) run: pytest tests/perf/test_long_prefix_moe.py::test_single_stream_long_prefix --profile --trace-output=/tmp/trace.pb
3) deploy model with env var RWD_ROUTER_BACKEND=cpu and monitor /metrics/debug/router_memcpy_count
4) toggle RWD_KV_PACK_STRATEGY=lazy vs eager and compare (eager triggers the double-copy)

Detailed actionable hypotheses and owners: 
- H1 (ownership: eng-serving-runtime / compilation): fused-attn fallback path triggers O(seq^2) temporaries for Mistral -> reproduce with smaller kernels, then change compiler flag to avoid fallback.
- H2 (ownership: eng-serving-runtime / memory): current KV packing code creates host-side contiguous buffers for interleaved-head models (Qwen) -> change to scatter/gather dispatch to avoid full temporary.
- H3 (ownership: eng-sre): batching window policy allows interleaving of long-context streams that cause synchronous router flushes; add jittering or backpressure to stagger long requests.
- H4 (ownership: eng-serving-runtime / router): router serialization format includes redundant metadata (timestamps + ids) that can be compacted; reduce per-token router payload.

Preliminary prioritization:
- Quick wins (1–2 days): compact router payload (H4), add KV pack lazy mode in staging (toggle only) (H2 partial)
- Medium (1–2 weeks): compilation flag tuning for fused-attn (H1), implement scatter dispatch for Qwen layout (H2 full)
- Longer (2–6 weeks): sustained load testing for relocated router (H3), integrate router decision caching across prefixes to reduce copy frequency

Metrics to monitor (suggested new metrics):
- router_memcpy_count (counter) and router_memcpy_bytes
- kv_pack_mode (gauge string) and kv_pack_temp_alloc_bytes
- transient_cuda_alloc_count and transient_cuda_alloc_peak_bytes
- python_gc_time_ms and python_free_list_churn_rate

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are we double-counting memory because of pinned vs pageable copies? Need raw cudaMalloc stats per allocator.
- Does the gated MoE routing state need to persist per-prefix (can we cache decisions per prefix hash)?
- Are there differences between int8-inference kernels for Qwen that avoid extra temporaries?

Next experiments (short runbook):
- EXP-F: enable router decision caching for repeated prefixes and rerun EXP-B/EXP-D
- EXP-G: compile Mistral with NO_FUSED_ATTENTION and compare median and tail latency at 8k/16k/32k sequences
- EXP-H: change Qwen KV packing to on-device scatter and measure memcpy reduction

Notes to reviewers / context pointers:
- This doc is intentionally rough; aim is to capture quick wins and direct pointers.
- See linked PR for trace-collection helpers: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/456
- Related ticket: JIRA-RINF-789 (investigate long-context memory spikes)

Checklist before we mark final:
- [ ] reproduce transient_cuda_alloc pattern with allocator debug on
- [ ] add temporary metric router_memcpy_bytes and verify in staging
- [ ] run sustained 24h soak with 10 concurrent long prefix streams
- [ ] get compilation team sign-off on NO_FUSED_ATTENTION experiment

Raw scratch (notes to self):
- Diego: follow up on whether the model loader is creating multiple views of KV for each expert (I think yes)
- Maya: can you add flamegraph sample from trace#1009 to the drive folder and tag it here?
- Liam: cheap mitigation: cap prefix length per request in hosted API, add explicit guidance in docs until root cause fixed

End of log.
